subject: SIG questionnaire follow-up: network controls (VPC peering, private endpoints, IP allowlists)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrate.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fintegrate.com>, Fintegrate Security <security@fintegrate.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: Network section clarifications (VPC peering / private endpoints)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the SIG submission earlier this week. Our network team reviewed the responses and had a few follow-up questions specific to your network architecture and evidence for the network controls section:

1) For customers on Redwood's hosted API, do you offer VPC peering or only private endpoints (PrivateLink/Private Endpoint) for direct connectivity? If both, how do you decide which to offer?

2) For customers opting for VPC peering (Dedicated or Private deployments), can you provide a sample peering diagram and say whether BGP or static routing is used? Any constraints around overlapping CIDRs?

3) For webhook callbacks and outbound requests, can you provide the list of egress IP ranges that Fintegrate can whitelist? Are those static per-region?

4) Any logs/screenshots you can attach showing a successful peering setup (exchange of routes, peering status) would be helpful.

Please send the answers and any attachments; we may follow up with a short technical call. Thanks — the team is aiming to close network questions by next Thursday.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Security Engineer, Fintegrate Payments
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Network section clarifications (VPC peering / private endpoints)

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. See answers inline below plus attachments we hope address the requests.

High-level summary
- Hosted API: we do not perform VPC peering into the Redwood-managed hosted tenancy. Instead, for private connectivity to hosted customers we offer region-specific Private Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint) and IP allowlist options. Private Endpoints are delivered as managed endpoints in the customer VPC and terminate into our private service network.
- Dedicated & Private deployments: VPC peering (or direct connect equivalents) is available for Dedicated and fully Private (VPC/on-prem) customers. Those modes support customer-controlled peering with route exchange.

Answers to numbered items:
1) Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: see summary above. Decision is primarily controlled by the deployment model the customer purchases — we don't peer into shared-hosted tenancies for security/isolation reasons.

2) Peering details for Dedicated/Private:
- We attach a sample peering diagram (redwood-dedicated-vpc-peering-diagram-20260202.pdf).
- Routing: we support both static route exchange and BGP (managed BGP over Direct Connect/Transit when customers require dynamic routing). BGP is recommended for large deployments.
- CIDR constraints: peered VPCs must not have overlapping IPv4 CIDRs. We can support /16–/28 prefixes; we recommend avoiding overly large overlaps and encourage customers to supply a /20–/24 for workload subnets.

3) Egress IPs for callbacks: attached is a CSV with the currently published egress IP ranges that hosted customers can use to allowlist webhooks (redwood-hosted-egress-ip-ranges-20260131.csv). For Dedicated deployments we can allocate a static egress NAT IP or a small pool per-customer; details are configurable at provisioning. Hosted egress ranges are region-specific and updated on a monthly cadence; customers should subscribe to the webhook on our status site for changes.

4) Evidence: we attached a zip with scrubbed peering logs and a sample successful peering exchange (security-evidence-peering-logs-20260131.zip).

Next steps: if you'd like a short call to walk the netops team through the diagram and BGP parameters, Marcus (cc'd) can join.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-egress-ip-ranges-20260131.csv; redwood-dedicated-vpc-peering-diagram-20260202.pdf; security-evidence-peering-logs-20260131.zip

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Trust & Safety Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Network section clarifications (VPC peering / private endpoints)

Thanks Soojin — quick follow-up from our network team after a quick review:

- For the Hosted egress IP list, can you confirm the update cadence and SLA for notifying customers of changes? We need 14 days notice for any changes that affect our allowlists.
- For Private Endpoints: do you support mutual TLS (mTLS) on the PrivateLink interfaces or should we expect to terminate TLS at your side only?
- For BGP: if we choose to use BGP, do you support AS path filters or prefix-lists for more controlled route advertisement?

Would be great if Marcus or someone from your network engineering team could respond to the BGP/peering specifics.

—Daniel
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fintegrate.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Network section clarifications (VPC peering / private endpoints)

Hi Daniel/Laura — Marcus from Infra (looping in Dev for routing specifics). Answers below: 

1) Egress IP cadence: For hosted egress ranges we publish a monthly CSV and notify subscribers via our status page and an email to the account owner. We can commit to a 14-day advance notice window for changes that require customer allowlist modifications; this is already a requirement for any change affecting published public IPs.

2) Private Endpoints and mTLS: Private Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint) terminate into our private service network. TLS is terminated at our service edge by default. If a customer requires mTLS to the service, we can enable mutual TLS on the service endpoint for Dedicated and Private customers as part of the provisioning process; for hosted PrivateLink endpoints we can negotiate mTLS on a per-customer basis but it requires a custom config and CA exchange.

3) BGP controls: We support BGP with MD5 auth and allow customers to request route filtering (prefix-lists / AS-path filters) during peering setup. We will advertise only the prefixes required for the service and can accept customer-specified filters; full details are captured in the peering playbook attached in the diagram PDF.

Operational notes: 
- Overlapping CIDRs: we will refuse peering where there is overlap; in some cases we can propose NAT or a transit approach if customers cannot re-CIDR.
- Ports: service endpoints require HTTPS (TCP/443). Peer management (BGP) uses standard BGP/TCP ports over the Direct Connect/transit link per provider.
- Monitoring: route telemetry and BGP session health are logged to our audit system; we can provide session up/down history (samples included in the peering logs zip).

If you'd like, we can run a short hands-on exercise (we provision a test peering and share live route tables). Proposed time: Thu 2026-02-05 10:00–11:00 PT — Marcus & Dev available.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
